title: Block bounds in Lean, Toffoli and column-mixing maps (13-14 October)
made_with: AI agents (Claude) directed by the author
notes: No person has read any of the proofs of this section.
'Proved in Lean' means the engine game of this repository and only the three standard axioms.
Savings are ln(mW/M)/ln m; finite-win savings follow OpenAI's finite-tensor paper.
Where notes disagree, the later skeptic verdict is used.

findings.statement: Theorem R for the engine's own words: for any subspace kept by every free letter, the total growth over the paid moves is at least what the targets need, so every unit needs at least W x demand / cap paid moves; singular mixing and garbage in scratch arrays are covered. It is a general form of the certificate lemma (the "FO lemma") of eumemic's pull request #288 in the community repository CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds.
findings.status_detail: only the three standard axioms; two AI skeptics rebuilt it independently; five deliberately broken versions failed to build

findings.statement: Block 4: every unit needs at least 41W/13 (about 3.154W) paid moves: the k = 8 hook at f = 9 has cap 27,456 and demand at least 86,592 = 16 x 5,412.
findings.status_detail: the counting theorem and the cap are proved in Lean; the demand is a 5,412 x 5,412 minor nonzero modulo 2,147,483,629, checked by a checker that shares no code with its generator; three programs by different agents found the same demand (one in floating point), a skeptic rebuilt it with its own code from exact minors, and the certificate program found the same rank; in the widened game it also rests on the keptness argument

findings.statement: Block 4: two moves in a row raise the hook by at most 48,576, and two moves in independent directions raise it by at least 48,576, so the value is exactly 48,576; three moves in independent directions raise it by at least 68,320; that three moves raise it by no more than 68,320 is not certified, so the engine-price cap of 0.176 holds only with high probability.

findings.statement: Depth lemma (family S): if every content holds at most one term of each input, two arrays need at least 2m moves at every block size, whatever the free group.
findings.status_detail: Farkas certificates checked by computer for every m, given b4-depth4's constraints; one skeptic's own program agrees on the hardest case

findings.statement: No hook, coordinate or cut certificate reaches 4 moves per array at any block size (hook family at most 4(n-1)/(n+2); coordinate certificates kept by all permutations at most 4(n-1)/n, argued by hand for m = 3 to 10; certificates that only the engine game keeps, such as lifts and affine-orbit sets, are not covered); so from block 5 on these certificates can never rule out a saving of 0.1 (about 0.16 at block 5, 0.24 at block 6 and 0.29 at block 7 stay out of reach).
findings.status_detail: upheld by three AI skeptics with label corrections; cuts: Theorem S' (two skeptics, theory-of-theories-and-logic)

findings.statement: At block 4 no screened family (hooks, two- and three-factor Venn sets, small affine shapes) reaches 3.5, so no hook or two-factor certificate can ever exclude 2 in 7 or 3 in 10; the k = 8 hook almost surely stops at 41/13.
findings.status_detail: screens computed; three codes agree on 86,592 against the upper bound 91,520 (argued by hand, re-derived by two skeptics); upheld with corrections

findings.statement: The best Theorem-R bound over all certificates (a relaxation over rank inequalities valid over C, including Dougherty-Freiling-Zeger) lies between 2.8 and 169/57 = 2.9649 at block 3 and between 3.154 and 3.94261 at block 4 (widened game); from block 4 on it is at most m - 0.0574.
findings.status_detail: exact certificates checked only by the track's own verifier; no skeptic

findings.statement: Ladder: reversal gives a unit with the same moves; beating 2.8 at block 3 needs c2 > 1.8 c1; excluding 2 in 7 at block 4 needs c2 > 1.75 c1 and c3 > 2.5 c1 (the block-4 hook has 1.77 and 2.49); Lambda^2 (x) Lambda^3 reaches c2 = 1.848 c1 but c3 = 2.515 c1; sums, mixtures, restrictions, single cuts, tensor squares and linear programmes over subspace dimensions give exactly Theorem R.
findings.status_detail: two AI skeptics upheld it; 1.848 confirmed exactly at two primes; the claim that excluding 5 in 14 or 2 in 7 'needs one of' a short list was corrected

findings.statement: Induction limits: projection from block 4 raises the bound by a factor of at most 1.1, pullbacks by less than 2, direct sums never beat their best part; whether the best Theorem-R bound grows with m is open.
findings.status_detail: upheld by two skeptics; 'general products are at most twice the best factor' was refuted by a skeptic's counterexample (true for constant dimension)

findings.statement: 'General products of certificate families are at most twice the best factor.'
findings.status_detail: by a skeptic's counterexample when the families' dimensions vary

findings.statement: Exact normal form: any run of moves on one array between two mixing steps equals free steps, the first r coordinate moves, free steps; so 'a unit exists' is one polynomial system over the group algebra; deciding 2 in 7 this way is out of reach.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic read it; programs not published

findings.statement: Toffoli, every address permutation and every phase pattern are free in OpenAI's RAM model if the engine gets an AND look-up table next to its XOR table (about 400 to 450 Lean lines, not written).
findings.status_detail: read from the Lean files and OpenAI's model; no skeptic was assigned

findings.statement: Toffoli and the other new relabellings buy nothing at blocks 2 and 3: the bounds 2 and 14/5 hold with them free.

findings.statement: One array at block 4 has 736,785 shortest routes in the widened game against 315 in the engine game (105 against 21 at block 3); the route set's symmetry group is the engine's affine group; the extra routes come from splitting into independent halves.
findings.status_detail: exact census; a skeptic confirmed it with an independent model

findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic upheld it and extended it to every single-term, single-register scheme

findings.statement: The flagship attempt to decide 3 in 8 at block 3 exactly: about 2.3e8 rational unknowns; new tools (per-input twist symmetry with 64 and 5 classes, a quotient game 256 times smaller, free finishing moves); every family searched empty; stopped once 14W/5 excluded the target.

findings.statement: 5 in 14 at block 3 is exactly tight on the hook (14 x 80 = 5 x 224) and not excluded in any game; in a tight one every move gains 80, no move's content is a single free image of an earlier output (gain at most 72), each input has at most two private moves, and the flagship's fresh-entry family is empty.
findings.status_detail: the structure facts are argued by hand and upheld by three AI skeptics; the gain table is checked by computer (certificate)

findings.statement: Term-by-term filter for a tight 5 in 14: only 30 of 135 frames can hold a term; for all 8 tight certificates the target looks exactly like 7 other targets, so no certificate argument can decide 5 in 14.
findings.status_detail: computed at two primes; no skeptic has read the proofs

findings.statement: A greedy 14-move program tight on all 8 certificates at f = 5 fails at f = 6 by 112 of 8,960 (0.175 of a move), all from one array's end condition; the per-array end condition at the next f is strictly stronger than the cheap tests.
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated; not published (it depends on pickled data)

findings.statement: 6 in 17 at block 3 is tight on no known certificate.

Of the assumptions behind the games, dropping 'free steps are monomial', 'the same map on every column', 'correct for every f' (beyond infinitely many f), 'exact correctness', 'independent inputs', 'the same unit at every level' and 'arithmetic over Q(i)' gains nothing (given Theorem R); exactness and linear arithmetic on the data are truly forced.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic for the assumptions table; parts were later argued again and upheld by AI skeptics in the Conjecture U round

findings.statement: At block 3 a partial paid move adds exactly its share of a whole move's cap (exact rank 20 for one fibre call), so partial moves open nothing there; block 4 untested.
findings.status_detail: one program, exact over Q(i), not repeated

findings.statement: The line between free and paid steps in OpenAI's model is work per entry, not linear versus non-linear; no loophole was found (data are only added, subtracted and scaled).
findings.status_detail: read from OpenAI's UniformFourier.lean and its two preprints; no skeptic

findings.statement: Chain maps (row ^= row << 1, row0 ^= row1 << 1 and their inverses) cost constant work per entry in OpenAI's model, a paid move seen through them is still one transform call per fibre, and the Fourier result carries over.
findings.status_detail: two independent simulators counted every operation (block sizes 2 to 4, up to 7 columns); the recursion argued by hand for every f and checked on raw arrays in 143 cases; one AI skeptic re-ran it

findings.statement: Correctness at every f is decided exactly by a weighted-automaton test; testing small f proves nothing (row0 ^= row1 << e composed with the transform agrees with it up to f = e and differs at e + 1).
findings.status_detail: exact over Q(i); a skeptic re-checked it
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: yes: every_f.py and ram_letters.py, identical output; data/chain-maps/rerun_2026-10-19.txt

findings.statement: With one chain map free, no subspace other than 0 and the whole space is kept by all free steps, so no Theorem-R certificate of the usual kind exists; a chain map and a shift give a one-column shift; a paid move seen through row ^= row << 1 contains a CZ chain between neighbouring columns.
findings.status_detail: exact at block 2 for f = 2 to 5 and at block 3 for f = 3; argued by hand for every f at block 2 by a skeptic

findings.statement: Block 2 with Clifford chain maps of the listed kinds that have a reading at alpha (or all at 1): at least 2 moves per array, by the 27 lines on a cubic surface (a perfect certificate) and two lemmas about readings.
findings.status_detail: two AI skeptics (both re-ran the 27-line computation; one checked the proofs and narrowed the scope); superseded by Theorem 2W

findings.statement: No certificate of the 27-line kind exists at the next readings (325 frames over the 16-element field, by Hirzebruch's inequality; 4,745 planes over the 8-element field, by Klein's classification).
findings.status_detail: upheld by a skeptic; richer certificates are not excluded

findings.statement: Chain maps repeating every 2 columns are the engine at block 4 with paired directions; a unit needs at least 1.7826 pairs per array, which excludes 2 in 3, 3 in 5 and 4 in 7; the remaining 5 in 9 is covered by Theorem 2W.
findings.status_detail: a skeptic recomputed the number with separate code and other primes; 5 in 9 by Theorem 2W (argued by hand, one skeptic)

findings.statement: With row ^= row << 1 free, the phase i^(parity of one row over all columns) equals (1+i)/2 + (1-i)/2 x (column-wide sign flip) at every f; so the f = 1 shortcut is invalid and any product-form certificate must be Pauli-blind.
findings.status_detail: checked by computer exactly up to f = 8 and by the automaton test; two AI skeptics upheld it
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: yes: lines27.py, relcheck.py and e2_counter.py, identical output; data/chain-maps/rerun_2026-10-19.txt

games: chain maps with a reading at 1

findings.statement: Block 3 with row ^= row << 1 or the running XOR free: the best certificate gives 231/131 = 1.763 moves per array (405 Fermat planes plus lifts, exact over Q(omega)); two natural constructions are capped below the 2.667 needed: 2.18 (Weil modules, computed) and 2.287 (keeping the Fermat planes, reproduced by a skeptic); lifts are capped only at 2.917 (a counting argument by hand), later lowered to 147/52 = 2.827 (theory-of-theories-and-logic), both above 2.667, so counting does not rule them out; 3 in 8 is open in this game.
findings.status_detail: the 1.763 certificate is checked by computer (counts re-run by a skeptic)

findings.statement: Weak bound for every cheap relabelling (chain maps, carries, affine maps of all address bits): if no mixing coefficient has an even denominator and the unit is correct at f = 2, it needs at least 1.5 moves per array at block 2 and 1.875 at block 3; it excludes no target.
findings.status_detail: checked by AI skeptics, one of whom wrote out a missing lemma

findings.statement: Searches with chain maps free found no unit (least squares for 2 in 3, 3 in 5 at block 2 and 2 in 5 at block 3; exact fixed-shape searches for 3 in 8 and 2 in 5).
findings.status_detail: evidence, not proof: the search found none of the existing units on 1,095 random 2-in-6 patterns; a skeptic rebuilt the least-squares search (99 of 99 checks) and re-ran it with a new seed; one apparent hit was a small-f artefact

findings.statement: Spare rows: in the game OpenAI's network lives in, rank-2 targets need 2W moves and rank-3 targets 3W, for every number of spare rows.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it by hand and tested 150 random words in each of four sizes

findings.statement: Spare rows, full game: certificates give 1.8485 (rank 2, 3 rows), 1.7692 (rank 2, 4 rows), 2.4883 (rank 3, 4 rows), floors 1.5 and 1.75; adding a row can only lower the best rate.
findings.status_detail: 1.7692 reproduced by a skeptic's separate code; 2.4883 from one code family; superseded for rank 2 by Theorem 2W' and a Venn certificate

findings.statement: Rank-3 target, 2 arrays in 5 moves with 4 spare rows: the best certificate gives 2.4883 moves per array, 0.012 short of excluding it.
OpenAI's finite-win game, Hadamard kernel on 4 and 8 entries: no word beats the plain call count (gossip bound 2N - 4; every dense 2 x 2 kernel).
findings.status_detail: a classical theorem applied; no skeptic

findings.statement: Hadamard kernel on 16 entries: 28 to 31 calls are open; every word with 31 or fewer calls avoids every layer-boundary state, so no Cooley-Tukey-shaped word can be shortened; the case reduces to one unproved inequality.
findings.status_detail: the reduction is argued by hand; annealing found nothing below 32 but failed to re-find a 32-call word, so it carries no weight; no skeptic

findings.statement: Zeta (subset-sum) kernel on 8 entries: no word with 11 or fewer calls exists, so Yates's 12 additions are optimal in OpenAI's finite-win game (11 calls would have saved 3.5e-2).
findings.status_detail: 5,528 of 6,828 output-order classes excluded by exact integer certificates, the other 1,300 searched exhaustively; one AI skeptic re-ran it and wrote an independent search for the hardest classes (its files were not kept)
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: yes: run_all.sh, 0 survivors at 11 calls over all 1,300 classes, 5,528 certificates valid; data/finite-win-game/rerun_zeta_2026-10-19.txt

findings.statement: Conjecture U: making more steps free (anything OpenAI's model does for a fixed amount of work per entry) never pushes a unit below 2, 2.8 and 41/13 moves per array at blocks 2, 3 and 4.
findings.status_detail: shown (argued by hand, upheld) for the classes in the next findings; block 2 later closed for every bounded game by Theorem 2W; Theorem E+ (theory-of-theories-and-logic) later covered Clifford chain maps with a polynomial inverse at blocks 2 to 4

findings.statement: Conjecture U holds for every column-uniform free step (any relabelling, Toffoli included, any phases) plus any fixed invertible operators on a few end columns: 2W, 14W/5 and 41W/13 at blocks 2, 3 and 4.
findings.status_detail: two independent proofs, each checked by two AI skeptics; 38 to 40 mixed words with random non-unitary end operators tested

findings.statement: Theorem R-infinity: the counting theorem needs correctness only at infinitely many f, given the trace condition and unitary steps; the phases need entries in Z[zeta8, 1/2].
findings.status_detail: upheld by AI skeptics; the field correction comes from a skeptic's counterexample (3 + 4i)/5
